basis: Defined by refeeding-induced electrolyte and fluid shifts; cardiac, neurologic and respiratory organ failure are not universal defining manifestations.
Primary dilation and dysfunction of the ureter; the renal axis includes ureters.
Inherited macular degeneration causing central visual impairment; manifestations are confined to the ocular axis.
Renal tubular transport defect with defining electrolyte depletion and metabolic alkalosis; QT prolongation and weakness do not establish lasting cardiac or muscle damage.
Familial hepatic portal vascular disease defined by portal hypertension; insufficient evidence supports additional organ damage in at least 30%.
Malignancy occupying the heart or blood vessels; other primary sites or metastatic organs are not consistent across this umbrella.
Inherited cone-rod retinal degeneration with reduced visual acuity in 4/4 reported patients.
Skeletal dysplasia defined by delayed epiphyseal and carpal ossification and abnormal hand bones.
AIPL1-related inherited retinal degeneration; a neurological ancestor does not establish additional brain or nerve involvement.
ALP deficiency causes profound skeletal hypomineralization; pulmonary hypoplasia and respiratory failure affect most liveborn infants with the lethal perinatal form.
Carcinoma in situ occupies pharyngeal epithelium; the specified pulmonary axis includes the pharynx.
Enlargement of ectopic thyroid tissue; tongue location does not change its endocrine origin. Dysphagia and airway obstruction are variable complications.
Carcinoma originates in exocrine pancreatic epithelium; metastases and secondary endocrine disorders are not assigned to this umbrella.
The supplied definition and ancestry identify an autoimmune nervous system syndrome with abrupt neurologic and psychiatric manifestations.
Y-chromosome rearrangement primarily affecting sexual development and fertility; consistent gonadal hormone failure or other axis damage is not established across subtypes.
Viral hemorrhagic fever with characteristic leukopenia, thrombocytopenia and bleeding; second-phase neurologic disease occurs in a minority.
Common origins are sinonasal/upper airway and oral/anorectal mucosa, together representing most cases; genital sites have no axis. Mucosal origin does not imply skin disease.
Developmental brain disorder; amyotrophy with elevated CK, optic disc pallor and eczematoid dermatitis each occur in 80-99%. Low IGF-1 alone does not establish endocrine failure.
Cerebral motor disorder causing hypotonia; reduced tone alone does not establish intrinsic skeletal muscle disease.
CDON-related forebrain malformation with developmental impairment; clefts and pituitary dysfunction lack evidence of qualifying frequency in this subtype.
Autoimmune melanocyte loss produces persistent cutaneous depigmentation; no additional organ damage is established.
GM2 storage causes progressive neurodegeneration; retinal ganglion-cell injury commonly causes visual loss (>30%). Cherry-red spots alone would not justify ocular involvement.
Structural aneurysmal disease of the thoracic aortic wall; adjacent-organ compression and rupture complications are not defining additional axes.
Autoimmune inflammatory polyarthritis with synovitis and progressive joint destruction; additional organ involvement is not common in this RF-positive subtype.
Syndrome defined by marrow failure and intellectual disability, each present in 6/6 assessed patients; short stature and hyperpigmentation alone do not establish other organ damage.
